correctness.rationale: For the specified infinite translation-invariant square lattice, the positive Bessel heat kernel has Fourier symbol -q(k)^s by Fubini/Tonelli and Gamma integration, q=4-2cos(k1)-2cos(k2) ranging over every value [0,8]. The 2x2 Bloch determinant gives lambda^2=V^2(4-q^s)^2-gamma^2. Thus for gamma>0 all fibers have real eigenvalues iff 0<s<2/3 and gamma<=V(4-8^s); for s>=2/3 the attained q=4^(1/s) gives a purely imaginary witness. For gamma=0 all 0<s<1 are real. q^s tends to 1 at every fixed q>0 but remains zero at q=0, yielding the positive minimal band-edge limit sqrt(9V^2-gamma^2) for fixed gamma<3V; the isolated origin fiber tends to sqrt(16V^2-gamma^2). Equality is an exceptional, generally defective fiber, not dynamical stability. Independent spectral inequalities and nonuniform limits corroborated numerically.
